headline: Chips Lead a Broadly Higher Tape as Geopolitical Anxiety Keeps Energy in Focus
body_html:
Midway through Tuesday's session, buyers hold a clear edge across the 520-name universe — 319 advancers against 197 decliners — with Semiconductors setting the pace at a gain of roughly 4.6%. Materials and Industrials are also trading well into the green, while Energy lags and Software edges fractionally lower, suggesting the session's enthusiasm is concentrated rather than uniform.

The dominant backdrop remains the US-Iran conflict and its reverberating effect on oil markets. Goldman Sachs placed Brent crude in an $80–$90 range contingent on the trajectory of a potential deal or further escalation, while BP reported quarterly profit doubling to more than $5 billion on the back of the oil-price surge. Aramco separately quantified the conflict's toll at 2.6 billion barrels removed from global supply — a figure underscoring just how structurally bid the energy complex remains even as OPEC+ output adjustments are seen as a near-term sideshow.

Into the close, watch the optical and networking cluster: Fabrinet and Coherent are both up double digits alongside Inspire Medical's standout 22.8% surge. On the downside, Certara and Bruker are nursing steep losses in healthcare tools, a pocket of stress worth monitoring for any late-session contagion into the broader healthcare tape.

briefs.headline: Inspire Medical Surges Nearly 23%, Leads All Movers
briefs.body: Inspire Medical Systems is the session's clear standout, jumping 22.84% to top the gainers board in the Healthcare-Devices space. No single macro catalyst is evident, pointing to a company-specific development — likely earnings or guidance — as the driver. The move stands apart from broader healthcare weakness elsewhere on the tape.

briefs.headline: Certara Drops More Than 19%, Biosimulation Sector Under Pressure
briefs.body: Certara is the session's hardest-hit name, shedding 19.19% and dragging attention toward the biosimulation corner of healthcare. Bruker compounds sector concern with a separate decline of 17.48% in life-science tools. The paired selloffs suggest investors are reassessing near-term growth expectations across healthcare instrumentation and analytics.

briefs.headline: BP Profit Doubles as Iran War Reshapes Energy Economics
briefs.body: BP posted quarterly profit exceeding $5 billion, a figure that roughly doubled year-over-year on the back of elevated oil prices tied to the US-Iran conflict. Aramco separately estimated the war has effectively removed 2.6 billion barrels from global supply, cementing the view that the conflict is the defining variable for energy markets this cycle.

briefs.headline: Goldman Sets Brent Range, Flags Deal or Escalation as Key Swing Factors
briefs.body: Goldman Sachs framed Brent crude in an $80–$90 corridor for the foreseeable future, with the bracketing conditions being either a US-Iran diplomatic agreement or a material worsening of hostilities. The bank's framing gives traders a clear scenario map at a moment when headline risk from the Strait of Hormuz remains acute.

briefs.headline: Iran Seeks Control Over Hormuz Traffic in Both Directions
briefs.body: A report citing sourced intelligence indicates Iran is pressing for supervisory authority over both inbound and outbound vessel movements through the Strait of Hormuz. The demand, if confirmed, would represent a significant escalation of Tehran's leverage posture and adds fresh uncertainty to tanker routing and insurance premiums across the Persian Gulf corridor.

briefs.headline: Palantir Surges on Exceptional Commercial Revenue Growth
briefs.body: Palantir Technologies vaulted roughly 16% after reporting commercial revenue described by analysts as exceptional in scale. The move is lending a tailwind to data-analytics and enterprise-software sentiment more broadly, even as the Software sector as a whole remains marginally in the red midday — a gap that underscores how concentrated the enthusiasm around Palantir specifically has become.
